ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
﻿A lampshade is made in the form of the lateral surface of the frustum of a right circular cone. The height of the frustum is $3\sqrt{3}$ inches, its top diameter is 6 inches, and its bottom diameter is 12 inches. A bug is at the bottom of the lampshade and there is a glob of honey on the top edge of the lampshade at the spot farthest from the bug. The bug wants to crawl to the honey, but it must stay on the surface of the lampshade. What is the length in inches of its shortest path to the honey?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the picture is a truncated-cone-shaped lampshade, the bug is at a point on the lower edge, and the honey is on the upper edge and is roughly located opposite the bug, at the farthest position. Unfold the lateral surface of the lampshade according to the specified method. The bottom radius is 6, the top radius is 3, and the vertical height is 3√3, so the frustum slant height is √((6−3)^2+(3√3)^2)=√(9+27)=6. Complete the frustum into a full cone; from the similarity relation, it can be obtained that the slant distance from the cone vertex to the top circle is 6, and the slant distance to the bottom circle is 12. After unfolding, an annular sector is obtained, with outer radius 12 and inner radius 6. The circumference of the bottom circle is 12π, so the sector angle is 12π/12=π. On the actual lampshade, the azimuth angle difference between the honey and the bug is π; when unfolded, a full 2π corresponds to sector angle π, so the angle difference in the unfolded diagram is π/2. Thus in the plane the bug is on the outer circle of radius 12, the honey is on the inner circle of radius 6, and the angle difference between the two is π/2. The straight line connecting the two points will pass through the missing inner disk, so it is not feasible. The shortest feasible path is: from the bug draw a tangent to the inner circle to the point of tangency, then go along the inner circular arc to the honey. The tangent length is √(12^2−6^2)=√108=6√3. The angle corresponding to the tangent point is arccos(6/12)=π/3, so the remaining inner-circle arc angle is π/2−π/3=π/6, and the arc length is 6·π/6=π. Therefore the shortest path length is 6√3+π.

method.method_draft: Unroll the frustum into an annular sector and solve the planar shortest path with a circular obstacle. From the text, take bottom radius 6, top radius 3, and vertical height 3√3, so the frustum slant height is √((6−3)^2+(3√3)^2)=6. Completing the frustum to a cone gives apex-to-top slant radius 6 and apex-to-bottom slant radius 12. Since the bottom circumference is 12π, the sector angle is 12π/12=π. The honey is farthest from the bug on the top circle, so its azimuth differs by π on the actual lampshade; in the developed sector this becomes angular separation π/2 because a full 2π revolution maps to sector angle π. Thus in the flat annular sector the bug is on the outer circle of radius 12 and the honey is on the inner circle of radius 6, separated by angle π/2. The direct chord crosses the missing inner disk, so the shortest admissible path is a tangent from the bug to the inner circle, followed by an arc on the inner circle to the honey. The tangent length is √(12^2−6^2)=6√3. The tangent point makes angle arccos(6/12)=π/3 from the bug’s radial line, leaving inner-circle arc angle π/2−π/3=π/6, whose length is 6·π/6=π. Total length is 6√3+π.

method.method_draft: Use the same cone development but find the contact point by optimization instead of invoking the tangent rule directly. Compute radii 3 and 6 and frustum slant height 6, so the developed frustum is an annular sector with inner radius r=6, outer radius R=12, and sector angle π. The farthest top point is opposite the bug around the axis, so in the sector the honey is at angular separation δ=π/2 from the bug. Let P be the point where the crawling path first reaches the top rim before possibly following the rim to the honey. If P has developed angular coordinate θ from the bug radial line, then a candidate length is L(θ)=√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)+r(δ−θ), with R=12, r=6, and 0≤θ≤δ, subject to the straight segment not cutting through the missing disk. Minimize: L'(θ)=Rr sinθ/√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)−r. Setting L'(θ)=0 gives √(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)=R sinθ, hence R cosθ=r, so cosθ=1/2 and θ=π/3. This is exactly the tangency threshold, so it is feasible and optimal. Then the straight portion has length √(144+36−144·1/2)=6√3, and the remaining top-rim arc has angle π/2−π/3=π/6 and length 6·π/6=π. Total: 6√3+π.

图像描述：图中是一个截头圆锥形灯罩，上口较小、下口较大；虫子在下边缘一侧，蜂蜜在上边缘相对于虫子绕轴最远的位置。虚线暗示虫子可能沿灯罩侧面爬行。

推理：顶部半径为 3，底部半径为 6，高为 3√3。截头圆锥的母线长为 √((6−3)^2+(3√3)^2)=√(9+27)=6。展开侧面后得到一个环形扇形。设展开图中内半径为 r、外半径为 R，则 R−r=6，并且上下圆周长比为 12π:6π=2:1，所以 R=12，r=6。扇形角满足 6·角度=6π，因此扇形角为 π。

蜂蜜在上边缘绕轴离虫子最远，即在实际圆周方向相差 π；展开图的扇形角 π 对应实际整圈 2π，所以虫子到蜂蜜的展开角差为 δ=π/2。

若路径先从虫子直线爬到上缘某点 P，再沿上缘爬到蜂蜜。设 P 与虫子径向线的展开角为 θ，0≤θ≤π/2。候选长度为 L(θ)=√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)+r(δ−θ)，其中 R=12，r=6，δ=π/2。求导得 L'(θ)=Rr sinθ/√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)−r。令 L'(θ)=0，则 √(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)=R sinθ。平方化简得 R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ=R^2(1−cos^2θ)，等价于 (R cosθ−r)^2=0，所以 R cosθ=r，即 cosθ=6/12=1/2，因此 θ=π/3。

此时直线段长度为 √(144+36−2·12·6·1/2)=√108=6√3。剩余上缘弧角为 π/2−π/3=π/6，弧长为 6·π/6=π。因此最短路径总长为 6√3+π。

直线段可行的条件是它不能进入缺失的内圆盘。设虫子点为 B、内圆点为 P，则在 P 处线段 BP 必须向外或与内圆相切，即 P·(B−P)≥0。由 |P|=r 且夹角为 θ，得 P·(B−P)=r(R cosθ−r)，所以 R cosθ≥r。代入 R=12、r=6，得 cosθ≥1/2；在 0≤θ≤π/2 内即 θ≤π/3。

候选路径长度为
L(θ)=√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)+r(δ−θ)。
求导得
L'(θ)=Rr sinθ/√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)−r。
并且
(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)−R^2 sin^2θ=(R cosθ−r)^2≥0，
所以 L'(θ)≤0；因此 L 在可行区间 0≤θ≤π/3 上随 θ 增大而不增，最小值取在最大可行角 θ=π/3。这时直线段正好与内圆相切。

直线段长度为
√(144+36−2·12·6·1/2)=√108=6√3。

method.CoT_final:
图像描述：图中是一个灰色的截头圆锥形灯罩，上口较小、下口较大；Honey 标在上边缘左侧附近，Bug 标在下边缘右侧附近，虚线表示虫子沿灯罩侧面爬行的可能路线。

推理：顶部半径为 3，底部半径为 6，高为 3√3。截头圆锥的母线长为 √((6−3)^2+(3√3)^2)=√(9+27)=6。把侧面展开后得到一个环形扇形。设展开图中内半径为 r、外半径为 R，则 R−r=6；又因为上下圆周长比为 6π:12π=1:2，所以 r:R=1:2，故 r=6，R=12。扇形角满足 r·角度=6π，所以角度为 π。

蜂蜜在上边缘绕轴离虫子最远，实际圆周方向相差 π；展开图的扇形角 π 对应实际整圈 2π，因此虫子与蜂蜜在展开图中的角差为 δ=π/2。

在展开图中，虫子在外圆上一点，蜂蜜在内圆上角差 δ 的点。由于内圆内部是被挖去的部分，虫子的路径不能穿过内圆盘。若直接连接虫子与蜂蜜，线段会进入内圆盘，所以最短可行路径应为：先从外圆点沿直线到达内圆上某点 P，再沿内圆弧到蜂蜜。取 P 与虫子径向线的展开角为 θ，其中 0≤θ≤δ。

直线段可行的条件是它不能进入缺失的内圆盘。设虫子点为 B、内圆点为 P，则在 P 处线段 BP 必须向外或与内圆相切，即 P·(B−P)≥0。由 |P|=r 且夹角为 θ，得 P·(B−P)=r(R cosθ−r)，所以 R cosθ≥r。代入 R=12、r=6，得 cosθ≥1/2；在 0≤θ≤π/2 内即 θ≤π/3。

候选路径长度为
L(θ)=√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)+r(δ−θ)。
求导得
L'(θ)=Rr sinθ/√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)−r。
并且
(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)−R^2 sin^2θ=(R cosθ−r)^2≥0，
所以 L'(θ)≤0；因此 L 在可行区间 0≤θ≤π/3 上随 θ 增大而不增，最小值取在最大可行角 θ=π/3。这时直线段正好与内圆相切。

直线段长度为
√(144+36−2·12·6·1/2)=√108=6√3。
剩余内圆弧的角度为 π/2−π/3=π/6，弧长为 6·π/6=π。
因此最短路径长度为 6√3+π。

蜂蜜在上边缘绕轴离虫子最远，即在实际圆周方向相差 π；展开图的扇形角 π 对应实际整圈 2π，所以虫子到蜂蜜的展开角差为 δ=π/2。

若路径先从虫子直线爬到上缘某点 P，再沿上缘爬到蜂蜜。设 P 与虫子径向线的展开角为 θ，0≤θ≤π/2。候选长度为 L(θ)=√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)+r(δ−θ)，其中 R=12，r=6，δ=π/2。求导得 L'(θ)=Rr sinθ/√(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)−r。令 L'(θ)=0，则 √(R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ)=R sinθ。平方化简得 R^2+r^2−2Rr cosθ=R^2(1−cos^2θ)，等价于 (R cosθ−r)^2=0，所以 R cosθ=r，即 cosθ=6/12=1/2，因此 θ=π/3。

此时直线段长度为 √(144+36−2·12·6·1/2)=√108=6√3。剩余上缘弧角为 π/2−π/3=π/6，弧长为 6·π/6=π。因此最短路径总长为 6√3+π。

raw_record.original_question: A lampshade is made in the form of the lateral surface of the frustum of a right circular cone. The height of the frustum is $3\sqrt{3}$ inches, its top diameter is 6 inches, and its bottom diameter is 12 inches. A bug is at the bottom of the lampshade and there is a glob of honey on the top edge of the lampshade at the spot farthest from the bug. The bug wants to crawl to the honey, but it must stay on the surface of the lampshade. What is the length in inches of its shortest path to the honey?
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the picture is a truncated-cone-shaped lampshade, the bug is at a point on the lower edge, and the honey is on the upper edge and is roughly located opposite the bug, at the farthest position.

Unfold the lateral surface of the lampshade according to the specified method. The bottom radius is 6, the top radius is 3, and the vertical height is 3√3, so the frustum slant height is √((6−3)^2+(3√3)^2)=√(9+27)=6. Complete the frustum into a full cone; from the similarity relation, it can be obtained that the slant distance from the cone vertex to the top circle is 6, and the slant distance to the bottom circle is 12. After unfolding, an annular sector is obtained, with outer radius 12 and inner radius 6. The circumference of the bottom circle is 12π, so the sector angle is 12π/12=π. On the actual lampshade, the azimuth angle difference between the honey and the bug is π; when unfolded, a full 2π corresponds to sector angle π, so the angle difference in the unfolded diagram is π/2.

Thus in the plane the bug is on the outer circle of radius 12, the honey is on the inner circle of radius 6, and the angle difference between the two is π/2. The straight line connecting the two points will pass through the missing inner disk, so it is not feasible. The shortest feasible path is: from the bug draw a tangent to the inner circle to the point of tangency, then go along the inner circular arc to the honey. The tangent length is √(12^2−6^2)=√108=6√3. The angle corresponding to the tangent point is arccos(6/12)=π/3, so the remaining inner-circle arc angle is π/2−π/3=π/6, and the arc length is 6·π/6=π. Therefore the shortest path length is 6√3+π.
